newsitem.title: USA: Clinton rating high despite campaign controversy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton rating high despite campaign controversy.

text.p: President Clinton's job approval rating remains high despite a steady series of stories about improper campaign donations to the Democratic Party, according to a Harris poll released Monday.
The poll showed that 57 percent gave him a positive job rating while 41 percent said he was doing fairly or poorly.

The poll was taken Feb. 19 to 23, a few days before the White House released documents that showed Clinton played a larger role than previously known in encouraging campaign donors to sleep in the Lincoln bedroom or get other perks.
A January poll had similar approval ratings for Clinton, which were near his all-time high of 59 percent in the Harris poll last September, two months before he was re-elected.

By contrast Democrats in Congress as a group received a 43 percent approval rating and 54 percent negative mark, only slightly better than majority Republicans who got a 38 percent favourable rating to a 58 percent negative rating.
House Speaker Newt Gingrich continued to get low marks -- 27 percent approval and 67 negative.

The Republican leader in the Senate, Trent Lott of Mississippi, continued to be little known, getting a 30 percent approval rate and 30 percent disapproval rating with 33 percent saying they do not know enough to rate him.
